whs-act-2020.title: Work Health and Safety Act 2020
whs-act-2020.abstract:
The Work Health and Safety Act 2020 is Western Australia's primary work health and safety legislation, which replaced the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1984. The Act commenced on 31 March 2022 and brings WA into the nationally harmonized WHS framework adopted across most Australian jurisdictions.

The Act establishes a primary duty of care for persons conducting a business or undertaking (PCBUs) to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers and others affected by the work. Officers (directors and senior executives) must exercise due diligence to ensure compliance with these duties.

Key provisions include worker representation through Health and Safety Representatives (HSRs), enforcement powers for WorkSafe WA including improvement and prohibition notices, and industrial manslaughter provisions for negligent conduct causing death. The Act covers all workplaces in WA except mines and petroleum operations.

whs-general-regs-2022.title: Work Health and Safety (General) Regulations 2022
whs-general-regs-2022.abstract:
The Work Health and Safety (General) Regulations 2022 provide the detailed regulatory requirements that support the WHS Act 2020 in Western Australia. These regulations specify how duties under the Act must be fulfilled and set out prescriptive requirements for various workplace hazards and situations.

The regulations cover a wide range of topics including management of risks, hazardous manual tasks, noise, plant and equipment, hazardous chemicals, construction work, confined spaces, and falling objects. They establish specific control measures and competency requirements that go beyond the general duties in the Act.

For traffic management and road work, the regulations are particularly relevant for construction work provisions, high-risk construction work requirements, and the management of mobile plant and equipment. Compliance with these regulations is mandatory and enforceable by WorkSafe WA inspectors.

osh-act-1984.title: Occupational Safety and Health Act 1984
osh-act-1984.abstract:
The Occupational Safety and Health Act 1984 was Western Australia's primary workplace safety legislation until it was repealed and replaced by the WHS Act 2020 on 31 March 2022. This Act had governed workplace safety in WA for 38 years.

While the Act is now repealed, it remains relevant for transitional provisions and understanding the historical framework. Some matters that began under the OSH Act may still be governed by its provisions during the transition period.

The Act established the general duty of care for employers and employees, requirements for consultation, and the powers of safety inspectors. It differed from the new WHS Act in several key areas including the use of 'employer/employee' terminology rather than 'PCBU/worker', and did not include officer due diligence duties or industrial manslaughter provisions.

mrwa-cop-2025.title: Traffic Management for Works on Roads Code of Practice
mrwa-cop-2025.abstract:
The Traffic Management for Works on Roads Code of Practice is the primary reference document for all traffic management activities on Western Australian roads. Published by Main Roads Western Australia (MRWA), this code establishes the mandatory requirements and standards that must be followed when conducting any work on roads.

The code adopts and adapts the Austroads Guide to Temporary Traffic Management (AGTTM) for Western Australian conditions. It covers the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved in traffic management, from Traffic Management Supervisors to Traffic Controllers, and establishes the requirements for traffic management plans, variations, and notifications.

Key topics include traffic guidance scheme requirements, signage standards, speed zoning, pedestrian management, mobile works, short-term low-impact works, and emergency setups. All Traffic Controllers must be familiar with this code as it forms the basis of competency requirements and legal compliance for traffic management work in WA. The May 2025 edition is the current version and supersedes all previous editions.

agttm-part-1.title: AGTTM Part 1 - Introduction
agttm-part-1.abstract:
AGTTM Part 1 introduces the Austroads Guide to Temporary Traffic Management series and establishes the overarching framework for temporary traffic management across Australia and New Zealand. It provides the context and principles that underpin all other parts of the guide.

The guide explains the purpose and structure of the AGTTM series, its relationship with other standards including AS 1742.3, and how the guide is adopted and adapted by different jurisdictions. It establishes key definitions and terminology used throughout the series, ensuring consistent interpretation across all parts.

Fundamental concepts covered include the safe system approach to road safety, the hierarchy of controls, risk management principles, and the roles and responsibilities of various parties in temporary traffic management. Understanding Part 1 is essential before delving into the more technical later parts, as it provides the conceptual foundation for why certain requirements exist and how the parts relate to each other. This part should be read by anyone new to traffic management or seeking a deeper understanding of the framework.

agttm-part-2.title: AGTTM Part 2 - Traffic Management Planning
agttm-part-2.abstract:
AGTTM Part 2 provides the framework for planning temporary traffic management on roads across Australia and New Zealand. It establishes the principles and processes for developing traffic management plans that maintain safety and traffic flow during road works.

The guide covers traffic management planning fundamentals including traffic flow analysis, capacity calculations, and delay assessments. It provides methodologies for determining appropriate traffic management approaches based on traffic volumes, road characteristics, and work activities. The planning process considers road user needs, worker safety, and the broader traffic network impacts.

Traffic Management Supervisors use this guide when developing Traffic Management Plans (TMPs) for complex or high-impact works. The guide provides the technical basis for decisions about lane closures, detours, contraflow arrangements, and work scheduling to minimize traffic disruption while maintaining safety.

agttm-part-3.title: AGTTM Part 3 - Static Worksites
agttm-part-3.abstract:
AGTTM Part 3 is the most frequently referenced part for Traffic Controllers working on static worksites. It provides comprehensive guidance on setting up and managing traffic control at fixed work locations where road workers and equipment remain in one place for extended periods.

The guide covers the full range of static worksite configurations including single lane closures, multiple lane closures, road closures with detours, shoulder closures, and median works. It details the requirements for advance warning, transition zones, buffer zones, and termination areas. Speed zoning requirements are comprehensively addressed, including the relationship between temporary speed limits and traffic management setups.

Specific requirements for excavations in the road, footpath closures, and works near intersections are included. The guide establishes minimum sight distances, taper lengths, and signage spacing based on speed zones. This part is essential reading for all Traffic Management Supervisors and forms the technical basis for most Traffic Guidance Schemes.

agttm-part-4.title: AGTTM Part 4 - Mobile Works
agttm-part-4.abstract:
AGTTM Part 4 addresses traffic management for mobile works where the work activity and traffic control devices move continuously or intermittently along the road. This includes line marking, vegetation control, road sweeping, and inspection activities.

The guide distinguishes between different types of mobile operations: continuously moving works, intermittent moving works, and works that move at intervals. Each type has different traffic management requirements based on the speed of movement, road environment, and risk profile. The guide covers the use of vehicle-mounted signage, shadow vehicles, and pilot vehicles.

Mobile works present unique challenges as the traffic management setup is constantly changing. The guide addresses the requirements for advance warning vehicles, spacing between vehicles, communication protocols, and the roles of personnel involved in mobile operations. It is essential reading for crews conducting any form of moving road work.

agttm-part-5.title: AGTTM Part 5 - Short Term Low Impact Worksites
agttm-part-5.abstract:
AGTTM Part 5 provides simplified traffic management requirements for short-term and low-impact works. These are works that have minimal impact on traffic and are completed quickly, typically within one shift, where the full requirements of Part 3 may be excessive.

The guide defines what constitutes short-term low-impact work based on duration, traffic impact, and road environment. It provides reduced traffic management requirements while still maintaining safety. Common applications include minor repairs, pothole patching, sign installation, and utility inspections.

The guide covers the use of simplified setups, reduced signage requirements, and specific provisions for different speed environments. It includes guidance on when short-term low-impact provisions can and cannot be used. Traffic Controllers must understand these limits to ensure the simplified provisions are not inappropriately applied to higher-risk situations.

agttm-part-6.title: AGTTM Part 6 - Field Staff Implementation
agttm-part-6.abstract:
AGTTM Part 6 is a practical implementation guide for field personnel involved in setting up, monitoring, and removing temporary traffic management. It translates the technical requirements of other AGTTM parts into practical on-site procedures.

The guide covers the day-to-day activities of traffic management crews including pre-start checks, equipment inspection, signage installation sequences, ongoing monitoring requirements, and pack-down procedures. It provides step-by-step guidance for common tasks and decision-making frameworks for unexpected situations.

This part is particularly valuable for Traffic Controllers and traffic management crew members. It addresses practical considerations like positioning of vehicles, communication methods, dealing with public inquiries, and responding to incidents. The guide complements formal training by providing a reference for field implementation of traffic management requirements.

agttm-part-7.title: AGTTM Part 7 - Traffic Controllers
agttm-part-7.abstract:
AGTTM Part 7 is the definitive guide for Traffic Controllers performing stop-slow baton duties. It establishes the competency requirements, operational procedures, and safety standards for this critical role in traffic management.

The guide covers the full scope of Traffic Controller duties including positioning, signaling techniques, communication protocols, and hazard awareness. It addresses the specific requirements for different work situations including single controller operations, multiple controller coordination, and night work. The guide also covers emergency procedures and incident response.

Competency requirements are detailed including the necessary training, assessment, and accreditation processes. The guide establishes the minimum standards that must be met before a person can work as a Traffic Controller. This part is essential reading for all Traffic Controllers and their supervisors, forming the basis for competency-based training and assessment.

agttm-part-8.title: AGTTM Part 8 - Processes and Procedures
agttm-part-8.abstract:
AGTTM Part 8 establishes the organizational framework for temporary traffic management including roles, responsibilities, and administrative processes. It defines the functional relationships between road authorities, contractors, and personnel involved in traffic management.

The guide details the responsibilities of key roles including the Traffic Management Designer, Traffic Management Supervisor, and Traffic Controller. It establishes the competency framework and certification requirements for each role. The processes for planning, approving, implementing, and auditing traffic management are comprehensively documented.

Administrative requirements including documentation, record keeping, incident reporting, and variations are covered. The guide also addresses the process for seeking approval to vary from standards and the risk assessment methodology required. This part is essential for understanding the governance framework and ensuring compliance with procedural requirements.

agttm-part-9.title: AGTTM Part 9 - Sample Layouts
agttm-part-9.abstract:
AGTTM Part 9 is a comprehensive visual reference containing sample Traffic Guidance Scheme layouts for a wide range of traffic management scenarios. It provides standardized diagram templates that can be adapted to specific site conditions.

The guide contains hundreds of sample layouts organized by work type and road environment. Categories include lane closures on multi-lane roads, single lane closures on two-way roads, shoulder closures, intersection treatments, pedestrian management, and road closures with detours. Each layout includes signage schedules, taper lengths, and spacing requirements.

These sample layouts form the basis for most pre-approved Traffic Management Plans including MRWA's regional TMPs. Traffic Management Designers use these layouts as templates, adapting them to site-specific conditions. The layouts illustrate the application of requirements from Parts 3, 4, and 5, showing how theoretical requirements translate into practical setups.

agttm-part-10.title: AGTTM Part 10 - Supporting Guidance
agttm-part-10.abstract:
AGTTM Part 10 provides supplementary guidance that supports the application of the other AGTTM parts. It addresses specialized situations, emerging issues, and provides additional technical information not covered in the main parts.

The guide covers a range of supporting topics including traffic management at special events, works near railways, works on bridges and structures, and traffic management in tunnels. It also addresses emerging technologies and their application in temporary traffic management, including electronic signage and intelligent transport systems.

Additional technical information includes detailed guidance on sight distance calculations, queue length assessments, and the impact of road works on heavy vehicles. This part serves as a reference for less common situations and provides the technical depth needed for complex traffic management scenarios. It should be consulted when situations fall outside the scope of the main AGTTM parts.
